tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis / What the recorded steps accomplish:
- Navigate to Magento admin customers grid URL.
- Encounter login page, then log in using username and password fields and Login button located by index/element hash (not shown as deterministic steps but recorded).
- Land on Manage Customers grid and analyze its structure (filters, pagination, mass actions, per-row Edit links, Add New Customer).
- Click a specific per-row Edit link (for customer ID 187, Jessica Chang) using an anchor element with element_hash 7c26516bad to open the customer detail/edit page.
- On the customer edit page, analyze structure: main action buttons (Back, Reset, Create Order, Delete Customer, Save Customer, Save and Continue Edit), tabs (Customer View, Account Information, Addresses, Newsletter, etc.), and sections (Account Information, Password Management, Addresses, Newsletter).
- Activate Account Information tab via its tab link (element_hash 15c034811f).
- Edit core account fields using input elements: First Name, Last Name, Email, and Group select (element hashes c97ae058b0, 987fc96142, 23374ff30a, 3ea20d8dee).
- Activate Newsletter tab via its tab link (element_hash 377d4eed8b) and toggle the newsletter subscription control (input element_hash dd8c60e0a0).
- Activate Addresses tab via its tab link (element_hash e10247917d).
- Edit address fields: Street Address, City, Zip/Postal Code, Telephone using inputs with element hashes 19a4d37557, c6a4ba6527, 30f018752a, 18910b9db1.
- Click Save Customer button (button element_hash b41a54f8ac) to persist changes.

Overall, the sequence demonstrates full flow for editing a customer from the grid, including login, navigation to customer edit, editing Account Information, Addresses, Newsletter subscription, and saving.

2) Task Definition / Purpose of the tool:
Create a reusable tool that, given Magento admin customer context, will:
- Navigate to the Magento admin customers grid (handling login with robust selectors to fix prior failure on input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]).
- Open a specific customer's edit page from the grid via their customer ID using the per-row Edit link pattern /edit/id/{customer_id}/.
- On the customer edit page, modify key customer attributes (first name, last name, email, customer group, website association) in the Account Information tab.
- Optionally modify one primary address record (street, city, postcode, telephone) in the Addresses tab.
- Toggle newsletter subscription in the Newsletter tab.
- Save the customer via Save Customer button.

This directly addresses the original goal: open a customer's detail/edit page from the grid and view/modify contact info, addresses, group, and newsletter subscription, then save.

3) Action Plan (deterministic steps):
A. Navigation & Login
- Step A1: navigation → Go directly to starting URL /index.php/admin/customer/.
- Step A2: wait → Brief wait to ensure page loads (login page or grid).
- Step A3: Agentic step to handle login robustly:
  - If login form is present, locate username input using label-based or partial-name selector (avoid brittle input[name='login[username]'][type='text']).
  - Input admin username and password (hard-coded credentials per instructions, NOT parameters).
  - Click Login button identified by text/value "Log in" or by being the only submit button in the login form.
  - Wait for navigation to Manage Customers grid.

We use an agent step here because previous attempts failed relying on a specific CSS input selector. The agent can flexibly use label-based/partial-name strategies described in the extracted login-page analysis. Authentication is fixed for this environment and not parameterized.

B. Open target customer via grid
Optimisation: Instead of clicking an Edit link in the grid UI, we can directly navigate to the customer edit URL because the link pattern is known: /admin/customer/edit/id/{customer_id}/.
- Step B1: navigation → Use URL operation based on current_url (admin base) to go directly to /index.php/admin/customer/edit/id/{customer_id}/.

This removes need for brittle grid selectors or row index logic and is fully deterministic given customer_id.

C. Edit Account Information
On the customer edit page, we rely on stable element hashes observed for the input fields and select:
- Step C1: click (deterministic) → Activate "Account Information" tab using elementHash 15c034811f (anchor tag, index 119). Even if content is visible across tabs, using the tab ensures context is correct.
- Step C2: input → First Name field (elementHash c97ae058b0) set to provided first_name.
- Step C3: input → Last Name field (elementHash 987fc96142) set to provided last_name.
- Step C4: input → Email field (elementHash 23374ff30a) set to provided email.
- Step C5: select_change → Group select (elementHash 3ea20d8dee) selecting by visible text group (enum: General, Wholesale, VIP Member, Private Sales Member).
- Step C6: (Optional website association) — based on recordings, Associate to Website select wasn’t directly interacted with; no elementHash captured. To avoid brittle inference, we will NOT manipulate website in this version of the tool.

D. Edit Newsletter subscription
- Step D1: click → Activate "Newsletter" tab (elementHash 377d4eed8b).
- Step D2: click → Toggle "Subscribed to Newsletter?" checkbox (elementHash dd8c60e0a0) to match desired boolean subscribed_to_newsletter. Because click is a toggle, we should use an agent step or assume initial state? No state introspection is available via deterministic steps. To keep the sequence deterministic, we will:
  - Use an agent step targeted to the newsletter subscription control that ensures it matches desired boolean (checking current checked state and clicking only if needed). That avoids double toggles without relying on hidden attributes in this schema.

E. Edit Address
- Step E1: click → Activate "Addresses" tab (elementHash e10247917d).
- Step E2: input → Street Address field (elementHash 19a4d37557) set to provided street.
- Step E3: input → City field (elementHash c6a4ba6527) set to provided city.
- Step E4: input → Zip/Postal Code field (elementHash 30f018752a) set to provided postcode.
- Step E5: input → Telephone field (elementHash 18910b9db1) set to provided telephone.

Country and State fields were visible in screenshots but not interacted with; we skip them to avoid guessing their element hashes.

F. Save Customer
- Step F1: click → Save Customer button (elementHash b41a54f8ac).
- Step F2: optional wait or extraction to confirm success message. For this tool, confirmation extraction is outside minimal essential steps, so we omit it per instructions.

4) Variable Identification / Input parameters:
Most data being edited should be parameterized; login credentials are fixed per instructions and should NOT be parameters.
Required vs optional based on UI semantics:
- customer_id (string, required): numeric customer ID used in URL /edit/id/{customer_id}/.
- first_name (string, required): First Name * is required in Account Information.
- last_name (string, required): Last Name * is required.
- email (string, required, format user@domain.com): Email * is required.
- group (string, required, enum ["General","Wholesale","VIP Member","Private Sales Member"]): Group * is required.
- street (string, required): Street Address * is required for address.
- city (string, required): City * is required for address.
- postcode (string, required): Zip/Postal Code * is required.
- telephone (string, required): Telephone * is required.
- subscribed_to_newsletter (bool, required): desired newsletter subscription state; the tool will ensure the customer subscription matches this.

We are not parameterizing less critical optional fields (prefix, middle initial, tax/VAT, DOB, fax, company, etc.) to keep tool focused on the core goal.

5) Step Optimization / Addressing prior failures:
- Prior failure: tool_view_customer.v3 attempted to use a deterministic navigation step combined with waiting for a CSS selector input[name="login[username]"][type="text"], which did not resolve, causing the whole tool to fail early. To fix this:
  - We use an agent step for login instead of a brittle deterministic selector. The agent will leverage the extracted analysis (e.g., label:contains('User Name') + input, input[name*='username'], etc.) and can handle timing/visibility issues.
- Optimization: Instead of clicking within the customers grid to find and click the Edit link, we navigate directly to /admin/customer/edit/id/{customer_id}/ once logged in. The pattern is confirmed by the recorded Edit link hrefs. This removes dependence on grid row index or text content.
- Deterministic element usage: For Account Information, Addresses, Newsletter, and Save Customer we rely on elementHash values captured during actual interactions (15c034811f, c97ae058b0, 987fc96142, 23374ff30a, 3ea20d8dee, 377d4eed8b, dd8c60e0a0, e10247917d, 19a4d37557, c6a4ba6527, 30f018752a, 18910b9db1, b41a54f8ac). These correspond to unique interactive elements already proven clickable.
- Newsletter toggle: A plain click step would always toggle, potentially ending in the wrong state. To keep behavior aligned with the subscribed_to_newsletter parameter while avoiding complex state inspection through this deterministic schema, we introduce an agent step specifically targeted at ensuring the control matches the requested boolean.
- No extra optional features: We do not include filtering, exporting, pagination changes, or mass actions on the grid, since they are irrelevant to the core task.
- URL Manipulation Pass 2: We apply URL navigation optimization only for opening the customer edit page (B1). Login is left to agentic handling due to POST/form submission, and the grid itself is not used.

Given all of this, the tool will:
- Be robust to login selector changes.
- Avoid the exact selector that caused v3 failure.
- Use deterministic element hashes for form interactions and Save Customer.
- Parameterize all key editable fields relevant to the original task.
name: tool_view_customer.v4
description: Open a Magento admin customer detail/edit page from the customers grid, modify key account, address, group, and newsletter subscription fields, and save the customer, with robust selectors that avoid prior login selector failures.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento admin customers grid URL (will redirect to login if not authenticated).
Allow time for the login or grid page to load.
Handle Magento admin login robustly using fixed credentials and label-based selectors, avoiding brittle input[name='login[username]'][type='text'] selector.
steps.task: If a login form is present on the current page, log in to Magento Admin using username 'admin' and password 'password123'. Locate the username and password fields using robust strategies such as labels ('User Name:', 'Password:'), partial name attributes (input[name*='username'], input[name*='password']), or id fragments (id*='username', id*='password'). Then locate and click the single submit control with visible text 'Log in' or type='submit' in the same form. Wait until the Manage Customers grid at /index.php/admin/customer/ is loaded (e.g., detect a table with id containing 'customerGrid' or a page title 'Manage Customers').

steps.description: Open the specific customer edit page directly using the known URL pattern and provided customer_id.
Wait briefly to ensure the customer edit page and its tabs/actions are fully loaded.
Activate the 'Account Information' tab in the Customer Information section so account fields are visible.
Set the First Name * field in Account Information to the provided first_name value.
Set the Last Name * field in Account Information to the provided last_name value.
Set the Email * field in Account Information to the provided email value.
Change the Group * dropdown in Account Information to the desired customer group.
Activate the 'Newsletter' tab so that the Newsletter Information section and subscription control are visible.
Ensure the 'Subscribed to Newsletter?' checkbox matches the desired subscribed_to_newsletter value, clicking it only if a toggle is needed.
steps.task: Within the current customer edit page, in the 'Newsletter Information' section, locate the control labeled 'Subscribed to Newsletter?'. Determine whether it is currently checked or selected. If its state does not match the desired boolean value {subscribed_to_newsletter}, toggle it (click) once to make the control match {subscribed_to_newsletter}. Do nothing if it already matches. Avoid changing any other newsletter filters or grid controls.

steps.description: Activate the 'Addresses' tab so that the primary address edit form is visible.
Set the Street Address * field for the primary address to the provided street value.
Set the City * field for the primary address to the provided city value.
Set the Zip/Postal Code * field for the primary address to the provided postcode value.
Set the Telephone * field for the primary address to the provided telephone value.
Click the 'Save Customer' button to persist all changes made to account information, addresses, and newsletter subscription.
